import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Prepare a more descriptive column for the 'has_video_4k' feature for the legend
df['has_video_4k_label'] = df['has_video_4k'].map({0: 'No 4K Video', 1: 'Has 4K Video'})

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create a figure and axes for the plot
plt.figure(figsize=(14, 9))

# Create a scatter plot to visualize the relationship between megapixels, price,
# sensor type, and 4K video capability.
# - x-axis: megapixels (quantitative)
# - y-axis: price_usd (quantitative)
# - hue: sensor_type (categorical, color-coded)
# - style: has_video_4k_label (categorical, marker style)
# - size: Adjust marker size for better visibility
# - alpha: Add transparency to handle potential overplotting
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='megapixels',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='sensor_type',
    style='has_video_4k_label',
    s=120,  # Increased marker size
    alpha=0.7, # Added transparency
    palette='viridis' # Choose a color palette
)

# Add a title to the plot
plt.title('Camera Price vs. Megapixels by Sensor Type and 4K Video Capability', fontsize=18, pad=20)

# Add labels to the x and y axes
plt.xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=14)

# Improve the legend placement and title
# The legend will combine hue and style legends automatically in seaborn.
plt.legend(title='Sensor Type / 4K Video', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0.)

# Add a grid for better readability of values
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)

# Adjust plot layout to make space for the legend
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.85, 1])

# Save the figure to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
